This is proven using ε-construction and Heine-Borel theorem, where left-continuity of f at each ai ensures existence of εi such that F₀ ⊂ ∪Ui. The key insight is that this construction mirrors measure-theoretic inclusion, where the finite measure v on S corresponds to a function f. Left-continuity of f implies that v({x}) = 0 for all x, establishing a duality between topological compactness and measure-theoretic regularity. The failure mode arises when f is not left-continuous, leading to potential gaps in interval coverage or non-measurable sets. The dual structure allows for both probabilistic inference (GSI) and dynamic system evolution (GSE) through measure-preserving transformations.
